     6	  229|   convention
     7	  230|   \[

    35	 2046| A time-block argument would have to carry both position and velocity. We
    36	 2047| establish a uniform estimate for the first variance coefficient with arbitrary
    37	 2048| deterministic initial phase. The covariance may be any member of the original

    44	 2055| tempered Radon covariance on $\R^3$, satisfying $\Gamma(rA) =

    46	 2057| x}\mu(\ud\xi)$. Put

    50	 2061|     R_\alpha=\frac{\alpha\pi V}{2\sin(\pi\alpha/2)},\\

    52	 2063|     b_\alpha=2^\alpha+\frac{3^{2-\alpha}}{2-\alpha},\qquad

    65	 2076|     &\le R_\alpha\lambda^{\alpha-2},

    36	TeX lines 2531-2553, proof 2555-2571 at a284420), one Gaussian mode per color: for colors
    37	`Fin m`, insertions `J_i v = g_i ⊗ K_i` (`gmul i (K_i v)`), frames `T_b` acting on `X`, a start
    38	vector `u`, per-color cutoffs `N_c` and a finite word `w` whose color counts are at most the
    39	cutoffs, the cut word (with `P = truncC Nc` before and after every insertion) equals the raw

    43	theorem cut_eq_raw_fock {X : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [InnerProductSpace ℂ X] {m : ℕ}
    44	    {B : Type} (K : Fin m → X →L[ℂ] X) (T : B → X →L[ℂ] X) (u : X) (Nc : Fin m → ℕ)
    45	    (w : List (Fin m × B)) (hN : ∀ c, counts w c ≤ Nc c) :
    46	    cut (truncC Nc) (fun i v => gmul i (fun l => K i (v l))) (fun b v => fun l => T b (v l))
    47	        (vac u) w =
    48	      raw (fun i v => gmul i (fun l => K i (v l))) (fun b v => fun l => T b (v l)) (vac u) w :=
    49	  cut_eq_raw GoodDeg _ _ (truncC Nc) (vac u) Nc (goodDeg_vac u)
    50	    (fun d i v hv => goodDeg_insert K d i v hv) (fun d b v hv => goodDeg_frame (T b) d v hv)
    51	    (fun d v hd hv => truncC_eq Nc d v hd hv) w hN
    52	
    53	end StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWordFock

1	# Statement ledger
     2	
     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
     6	the manuscript revision a284420, and labels are written exactly as in its
     7	LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
     8	and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98, 3920258 and
     9	975feb3. Revision a284420 makes two mathematical edits that the ledger
    10	follows. (1) In `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` it adds Lemma
    11	`L:spatial-fourier-bound` (lines 101-164, display `E:spatial-fourier-bound`),
    12	the deterministic bound `A_sp(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_alpha b^(alpha/2)` that
    13	`SpatialFourierBound` already proved, and the proof of
    14	`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (same label and statement) now derives `R_0 < inf`
    15	from it, independently of the finiteness of `S_1^pos`, which it keeps only
    16	for the score inequality. (2) In the main file, `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
    17	replaces its smoothing and truncation sentence by the multiplier comparison
    18	`E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (a measurable multiplier `m` in `[0,1]`,
    19	nested measurable Laplace domains, positivity after time integration,
    20	scaling asserted only for the original covariance) and its proof by the
    21	corresponding argument. The other changes since 975feb3 are prose and front
    22	matter (title, abstract, preface, a theory-outlook chapter, the reader
    23	edition, Appendices F and G, the list of notation moved to the back).
    24	Every cited label exists exactly once at a284420. Three of them are new at
    25	a284420 and do not exist at 975feb3: `L:spatial-fourier-bound`,
    26	`E:spatial-fourier-bound` and `E:damped-multiplier-comparison`. Every other
    27	cited label exists exactly once, in the same file, at both revisions, and
    28	every such cited lemma, proposition, theorem, equation and section has the
    29	same statement and proof up to whitespace and braces, except
    30	`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (proof only), `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
    31	(statement and proof) and the section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
    32	(the new lemma). TeX line numbers were moved to a284420 by a line map; each
    33	moved range has the same text at both revisions, and the ranges inside the
    34	two edited passages were mapped to the corresponding new passages by hand
    35	(script checks recorded in `provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).
    36	
    37	## Scope
    38	
    39	- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
    40	  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
    41	  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean` (step modules) or
    42	  `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/<Module>.lean` (whole-result modules);
    43	  `Audit/<module>/` prints the elaborated types.
    44	- The rows cover every public theorem (2050) and 418 definitions whose
    45	  values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other 89
    46	  public definitions have no rows of their own: 85 (for example `kappa`,
    47	  `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`, `InventoryProduct.partialEval`,
    48	  `OccupationPhysicalClass.volI`, `SpaceTimePositivity.timeMeasure`,
    49	  `TerminalWick.chainMassReal`, `WaveGreenFourier.spherePhi` and
    50	  `OccupationCeilingExact.stepG`) only name quantities or measures used in
    51	  those statements, and four are the instances that make
    52	  `TimeCompletion.Pre` a pre-inner-product space; read their bodies in the
    53	  Lean source or in `Audit/`.
    54	- The `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules check finite, algebraic and scalar
    55	  steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates,
    56	  real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional
    57	  inner-product and finite-word facts. The exception is `HermiteWordFock`
    58	  (wave L9), which applies `HermiteWord.cut_eq_raw` to the Fock model of
    59	  `FockForm` and so formalizes `L:finite-word-cutoff` with one Gaussian
    60	  coordinate per color (section "HermiteWordFock (whole result)").
    61	- The seventy-six `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment` modules (sections marked
    62	  "whole result" below; four of them are the wave-kernel and time-fractional
    63	  foundation of `ClockCopy`, `GaussianTest` is the Gaussian-test foundation
    64	  of `MaskedSpectralGrowth`, and `VariationalFloor` and `SeriesType` are
    65	  foundations added in wave L6, `H1Density` one added in wave L7,
    66	  `FiniteWick` (the finite Wick formula) one added in wave L8, and
    67	  `GaussianHermite` and `HermiteFock` (normalized Hermite polynomials and the

  2288	\begin{lemma}[A complex phase bound]\label{L:complex-phase}
  2289	  Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $A_0$ a bounded nonnegative selfadjoint
  2290	  operator, and $B$ a bounded selfadjoint operator. Write $A_\rho = \rho^2+A_0$.
  2291	  Suppose that, for $0 < a < 1$ and $d > 0$,
  2292	  \begin{equation}\label{E:abstract-sandwich}
  2293	    \|A_\rho^{-1/2}BA_\rho^{-1/2}\|\le d\rho^{a-2},
  2294	    \qquad \rho>0.
  2295	  \end{equation}
  2296	  Put
  2297	  \[
  2298	    I_a=\int_0^\infty s^{-1/2}(1+s)^{(a-3)/2}\ud s,\qquad
  2299	    \delta_a=\min\{1/4,\pi/(8I_a)\}.
  2300	  \]
  2301	  For $\lambda > 0$ and $|z| \le \delta_a\lambda^{2-a}/d$, let $L = A_0-zB$. The
  2302	  phase propagator of $u''+Lu = 0$ satisfies
  2303	  \begin{equation}\label{E:complex-phase-bound}
  2304	    \|\mathcal{M}_z(h)\|_{X_\lambda\to X_\lambda}
  2305	    \le100e^{2\lambda h},\qquad
  2306	    \|(f,g)\|_{X_\lambda}^2
  2307	    =\|f\|^2+\|A_\lambda^{-1/2}g\|^2,\quad h\ge0.
  2308	  \end{equation}
  2309	  The constant is independent of $H$, $\|A_0\|$ and $\|B\|$.
  2310	\end{lemma}
  2311	
  2312	\begin{proof}
  2313	  Set $\delta = \delta_a$ and $L_\lambda = L+\lambda^2$. For $\kappa =
  2314	  (\lambda^2+t)^{1/2}$,
  2315	  \[
  2316	    L_\lambda+t
  2317	    =A_\kappa^{1/2}(1-zK_\kappa)A_\kappa^{1/2},\qquad
  2318	    K_\kappa=A_\kappa^{-1/2}BA_\kappa^{-1/2}.
  2319	  \]
  2320	  Since $a-2 < 0$, $\|zK_\kappa\| \le \delta$. Thus, these operators are
  2321	  invertible and
  2322	  \[
  2323	    \|A_\kappa^{1/2}(L_\lambda+t)^{-1}\|
  2324	    \le\frac1{(1-\delta)\kappa}.
  2325	  \]
  2326	  Also $\operatorname{Re}\langle L_\lambda u,u\rangle \ge (1-\delta)\langle
  2327	  A_\lambda u,u\rangle$.
  2328	
  2329	  Principal inverse square roots are defined on the right half-plane. The scalar
  2330	  identity $w^{-1/2} = \pi^{-1}\int_0^\infty t^{-1/2}(w+t)^{-1}\ud t$, and
  2331	  bounded holomorphic calculus, give
  2332	  \[
  2333	    Q_z-1
  2334	    =\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty t^{-1/2}A_\lambda^{1/2}
  2335	    \big[(L_\lambda+t)^{-1}-(A_\lambda+t)^{-1}\big]\ud t,
  2336	    \qquad Q_z=A_\lambda^{1/2}L_\lambda^{-1/2}.
  2337	  \]
  2338	  The integrals converge in operator norm. Indeed, the resolvent identity,
  2339	  $\|A_\lambda^{1/2}A_\kappa^{-1/2}\| \le 1$, and the following ordered
  2340	  factorization give the required integrand bound:
  2341	  \[
  2342	    \begin{split}
  2343	      &A_\lambda^{1/2}
  2344	      \big[(L_\lambda+t)^{-1}-A_\kappa^{-1}\big]\\
  2345	      &\qquad=A_\lambda^{1/2}A_\kappa^{-1/2}
  2346	      (1-zK_\kappa)^{-1}zK_\kappa A_\kappa^{-1/2}.
  2347	    \end{split}
  2348	  \]
  2349	  The four factors have norms at most $1$, $(1-\delta)^{-1}$, $|z|d\kappa^{a-2}$
  2350	  and $\kappa^{-1}$, respectively. Thus, the integrand without $t^{-1/2}/\pi$ is
  2351	  bounded by
  2352	  \[
  2353	    \frac{|z|d}{1-\delta}\kappa^{a-3}.
  2354	  \]
  2355	  Consequently,
  2356	  \[
  2357	    \|Q_z-1\|
  2358	    \le\frac{|z|d\lambda^{a-2}I_a}{\pi(1-\delta)}
  2359	    \le\frac16.
  2360	  \]
  2361	  In particular, $Q_z$ and $Q_z^{-1}$ have norm at most two. Apply the same
  2362	  argument to $L^* = A_0-\overline zB$ and take adjoints. It follows that all
  2363	  four operators
  2364	  \begin{equation}\label{E:phase-root-comparisons}
  2365	    A_\lambda^{1/2}L_\lambda^{-1/2},\quad
  2366	    L_\lambda^{-1/2}A_\lambda^{1/2},\quad
  2367	    L_\lambda^{1/2}A_\lambda^{-1/2},\quad
  2368	    A_\lambda^{-1/2}L_\lambda^{1/2}
  2369	  \end{equation}
  2370	  have norm at most two. This is a quantitative comparison at the bounded
  2371	  cutoffs, not an assumed square-root domain identity.
  2372	
  2373	  We next control the numerical range. For $\|u\| = 1$ put $s = \|A_0^{1/2}u\|$.
  2374	  Optimizing~\eqref{E:abstract-sandwich} at $\rho = s$ gives $|\langle
  2375	  Bu,u\rangle| \le 2ds^a$. If $s = 0$, the same conclusion follows by letting
  2376	  $\rho\downarrow0$. Separately, evaluating~\eqref{E:abstract-sandwich} at $\rho
  2377	  = \lambda$ gives
  2378	  \[
  2379	    |\langle Bu,u\rangle|
  2380	    \le d\lambda^{a-2}(s^2+\lambda^2),\qquad
  2381	    |z\langle Bu,u\rangle|\le\delta(s^2+\lambda^2).
  2382	  \]
  2383	  This is the estimate for the real part; the optimized estimate controls the
  2384	  imaginary part. Thus, for $w = x+iy = \langle Lu,u\rangle$,
  2385	  \[
  2386	    x+\lambda^2\ge(1-\delta)(s^2+\lambda^2),\qquad
  2387	    |y|\le2\delta\lambda^{2-a}s^a.
  2388	  \]
  2389	  Since $s^{2a}\lambda^{2-2a} \le s^2+\lambda^2$,
  2390	  \[
  2391	    y^2\le\frac{4\delta^2}{1-\delta}\lambda^2(x+\lambda^2)
  2392	    \le\frac13\lambda^2(x+\lambda^2),\qquad
  2393	    x\ge-\lambda^2/4.
  2394	  \]
  2395	  Hence, $|w| \le x+2\lambda^2$, and either square root of $w$ has
  2396	  $|\operatorname{Im}\sqrt w| \le \lambda$.
  2397	
  2398	  The scalar functions
  2399	  \[
  2400	    C_h(w)=\cos(h\sqrt w),\qquad
  2401	    F_h(w)=\sqrt{w+\lambda^2}\frac{\sin(h\sqrt w)}{\sqrt w},\qquad
  2402	    H_h(w)=\frac{w}{\sqrt{w+\lambda^2}}
  2403	    \frac{\sin(h\sqrt w)}{\sqrt w}
  2404	  \]
  2405	  are holomorphic on a neighborhood of $\overline{W(L)}$. The values at $w = 0$
  2406	  are removable; the only square-root branch required is that of $w+\lambda^2$,
  2407	  whose real part is positive. On the numerical range,
  2408	  \[
  2409	    |C_h(w)|\le e^{\lambda h},\qquad
  2410	    |F_h(w)|\le2(1+\lambda h)e^{\lambda h},\qquad
  2411	    |H_h(w)|\le2e^{\lambda h}.
  2412	  \]
  2413	  Indeed, $|\operatorname{Im}\sqrt w| \le \lambda$ gives $|\cos(h\sqrt
  2414	  w)|,|\sin(h\sqrt w)| \le e^{\lambda h}$. The entire identity $\sin(h\sqrt
  2415	  w)/\sqrt w = \int_0^h\cos(r\sqrt w)\ud r$ also gives the bound $he^{\lambda
  2416	  h}$, including $w = 0$. If $|w| \le \lambda^2/2$, then
  2417	  \[
  2418	    |F_h(w)|\le\sqrt{3/2}\,\lambda h e^{\lambda h}.
  2419	  \]
  2420	  If $|w| > \lambda^2/2$, then $|w+\lambda^2|/|w| \le 3$, so $|F_h(w)| \le
  2421	  \sqrt3 e^{\lambda h}$. These bounds imply the displayed estimate for $F_h$.
  2422	  Finally,
  2423	  \[
  2424	    \frac{|w|}{|w+\lambda^2|}
  2425	    \le1+\frac{\lambda^2}{|w+\lambda^2|}
  2426	    \le1+(1-\delta)^{-1}\le7/3,
  2427	  \]
  2428	  and $H_h(w) = \sqrt w\sin(h\sqrt w)/\sqrt{w+\lambda^2}$ gives its stated
  2429	  bound. All identities have their removable values at zero. Applying the
  2430	  imported~\eqref{E:cp-input} gives bounds $3e^{\lambda h}$, $6(1+\lambda
  2431	  h)e^{\lambda h}$ and $6e^{\lambda h}$ for these three operator functions.
  2432	
  2433	  Under the isometry $(u,v)\mapsto(u,A_\lambda^{-1/2}v)$, the four phase blocks
  2434	  are
  2435	  \[
  2436	    C_h(L),\quad
  2437	    F_h(L)L_\lambda^{-1/2}A_\lambda^{1/2},\quad
  2438	    -A_\lambda^{-1/2}L_\lambda^{1/2}H_h(L),\quad
  2439	    A_\lambda^{-1/2}L_\lambda^{1/2}C_h(L)
  2440	    L_\lambda^{-1/2}A_\lambda^{1/2}.
  2441	  \]
  2442	  This is the usual matrix
  2443	  $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}C_h(L)&G_h(L)\\-LG_h(L)&C_h(L)\end{smallmatrix}\right)$,
  2444	  with $G_h(w) = \sin(h\sqrt w)/\sqrt w$, after weighting. In the order
  2445	  displayed, the four block norms are at most
  2446	  \[
  2447	    3e^{\lambda h},\qquad
  2448	    12(1+\lambda h)e^{\lambda h},\qquad
  2449	    12e^{\lambda h},\qquad12e^{\lambda h}.
  2450	  \]
  2451	  For example, the last block has two root-comparison factors of norm at most
  2452	  two, with $C_h(L)$ between them. Only functions of $L$ commute; no commutation
  2453	  with $A_\lambda$ is used in these ordered products. A block operator on
  2454	  $H\oplus H$ has norm at most the sum of its four block norms, by the triangle
  2455	  inequality and the norm-one coordinate inclusions and projections. Therefore,
  2456	  its norm is at most
  2457	  \[
  2458	    (39+12\lambda h)e^{\lambda h}
  2459	    \le39(1+\lambda h)e^{\lambda h}\le100e^{2\lambda h}.
  2460	  \]
  2461	  The phase operator itself is the exponential of the bounded block generator
  2462	  with rows $(0,1)$ and $(-L,0)$. It is entire in $z$; the intermediate square
  2463	  roots are used to estimate it, not to impose a branch-dependent definition of
  2464	  that entire operator. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:complex-phase}.
  2465	\end{proof}

2472	\begin{lemma}[Gaussian cutoff form bound]\label{L:fock-form}
  2473	  Retain the covariance and $R_\alpha$ of Section~\ref{S:static-phase}. Fix
  2474	  $\epsilon > 0$. Represent the smoothed real field on independent standard
  2475	  Gaussian coordinates as $W_\epsilon(x) = \sum_{i\ge1}g_i e_i(x)$ in
  2476	  $L^2(\Omega)$. Let $P_N$ be projection onto Gaussian Hermite degrees at most
  2477	  $N$, and $S_b$ spatial Fourier projection onto $|\eta| \le b$. For finite $m$,
  2478	  on their joint range set
  2479	  \[
  2480	    B_{N,m,b}=P_NS_b\Big(\sum_{i=1}^m g_i M_{e_i}\Big)S_bP_N,\qquad
  2481	    A_\rho=\rho^2-\Delta .
  2482	  \]
  2483	  These are bounded selfadjoint operators and, uniformly in $\epsilon,m,b$,
  2484	  \begin{equation}\label{E:fock-sandwich}
  2485	    \|A_\rho^{-1/2}B_{N,m,b}A_\rho^{-1/2}\|
  2486	    \le d_N\rho^{\alpha/2-2},\qquad
  2487	    d_N=2\sqrt{N+1}\sqrt{R_\alpha}.
  2488	  \end{equation}
  2489	\end{lemma}
  2490	
  2491	\begin{proof}
  2492	  Choose an orthonormal basis of the real isonormal space, which is separable,
  2493	  and write $e_i(x) = \E[W_\epsilon(x)g_i]$. Then $\sum_i e_i(x)^2 =
  2494	  \Gamma_\epsilon(0) = :v_\epsilon$, and $|e_i(x)| \le \sqrt{v_\epsilon}$. Thus,
  2495	  each multiplication $M_{e_i}$ is bounded and selfadjoint. Put $H_i =
  2496	  A_\rho^{-1/2}M_{e_i}A_\rho^{-1/2}$ on spatial $L^2$. Gaussian isometry and
  2497	  spatial Plancherel give
  2498	  \[
  2499	    \sum_i\|H_i f\|_2^2
  2500	    =\frac1{(2\pi)^3}\int
  2501	    \frac{|\widehat{f}(\eta)|^2}{\rho^2+|\eta|^2}
  2502	    J_{\rho,\epsilon}(\eta)\ud\eta,\qquad
  2503	    J_{\rho,\epsilon}(\eta)
  2504	    =\int\frac{e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi)}
  2505	    {\rho^2+|\eta+\xi|^2}.
  2506	  \]
  2507	  This is the covariance calculation for $A_\rho^{-1/2}W_\epsilon
  2508	  A_\rho^{-1/2}f$. By Lemma~\ref{L:phase-contractions}, $J_{\rho,\epsilon} \le
  2509	  R_\alpha\rho^{\alpha-2}$. Therefore, $\sum_i H_i^2 \le
  2510	  R_\alpha\rho^{\alpha-4}I$ in quadratic forms. Finite sums have the same upper
  2511	  bound. Compression to $S_b$ preserves it: for selfadjoint $H_i$,
  2512	  $(S_bH_iS_b)^2 \le S_bH_i^2S_b$ on its range. Both row and column variances
  2513	  are the same, since these operators are selfadjoint.
  2514	
  2515	  For completeness, use normalized Hermite polynomials, so multiplication by
  2516	  $g_i$ is $a_i^*+a_i$, with $g_i h_k =
  2517	  \sqrt{k_i+1}\,h_{k+e_i}+\sqrt{k_i}\,h_{k-e_i}$. On degree $k$, the row map
  2518	  $(v_i)\mapsto\sum_i a_i^*v_i$ has norm $\sqrt{k+1}$: its product with its

  2531	\begin{lemma}[Exact cutoffs for finite Gaussian words]\label{L:finite-word-cutoff}
  2532	  Let $g_{ij}$, $1 \le i \le M$, $1 \le j \le m_i$, be independent standard real
  2533	  Gaussian coordinates, grouped by color $i$, and let $\mathscr{X}$ be a complex
  2534	  Hilbert space. On Gaussian polynomials with coefficients in $\mathscr{X}$ set
  2535	  \[
  2536	    J_i=\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}M_{g_{ij}}\otimes K_{ij},
  2537	  \]
  2538	  where each $K_{ij}$ is bounded on $\mathscr{X}$. Let $F_0,\ldots,F_n$ be
  2539	  bounded operators acting only on $\mathscr{X}$. Fix a word $i_1,\ldots,i_n$,
  2540	  and let $r_i$ be the number of its occurrences of color $i$. If $N_i \ge r_i$
  2541	  and $P$ projects each color onto total Hermite degree at most $N_i$, then, for
  2542	  every $v \in \mathscr{X}$,
  2543	  \begin{equation}\label{E:finite-word-cutoff}
  2544	    \begin{split}
  2545	      &(I\otimes F_n)(PJ_{i_n}P)(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
  2546	      (PJ_{i_1}P)(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v)\\
  2547	      &\qquad=(I\otimes F_n)J_{i_n}(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
  2548	      J_{i_1}(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v).
  2549	    \end{split}
  2550	  \end{equation}
  2551	  The equality holds for finite sums and for Bochner integrals of such words
  2552	  whenever the displayed vector integrals exist.
  2553	\end{lemma}
  2554	
  2555	\begin{proof}
  2556	  In normalized Hermite coordinates, multiplication by $g_{ij}$ maps
  2557	  $h_{\boldsymbol a}$ to $\sqrt{a_{ij}+1}\,h_{\boldsymbol a+e_{ij}}
  2558	  +\sqrt{a_{ij}}\,h_{\boldsymbol a-e_{ij}}$; the second term is zero if $a_{ij}
  2559	  = 0$. Thus, it changes the total degree of color $i$ by one and leaves all
  2560	  other color degrees unchanged. The operators $I\otimes F_l$ leave every
  2561	  Gaussian degree unchanged. After the first $l$ insertions, the uncompressed
  2562	  word therefore has color-$i$ degree at most $r_i(l) = |\{j\le l:i_j=i\}| \le
  2563	  r_i \le N_i$. This is an induction starting from degree zero in every color.
  2564	  Consequently, $P$ is the identity both before and after every insertion along
  2565	  that word. Induction on $l$ now proves \eqref{E:finite-word-cutoff}. The
  2566	  lowering term has been retained: the assertion includes creation followed by
  2567	  annihilation and all resulting self-contractions. Linearity and equality of
  2568	  the vector integrands prove the last assertion. This is an equality of
  2569	  selected finite words, not of full propagators at a fixed cutoff. This proves
  2570	  Lemma~\ref{L:finite-word-cutoff}.
  2571	\end{proof}

  2164	\begin{proposition}[First variance estimate for arbitrary phase]
  2165	  \label{P:static-phase-variance}
  2166	  Let $N = \|(f,g)\|_\lambda$. Uniformly in $\epsilon > 0$,
  2167	  \begin{align}
  2168	    \E\|Z_1(h)\|_\lambda^2
  2169	    &\le R_\alpha h^2\lambda^{\alpha-2}
  2170	    (1+\lambda^2h^2)^2N^2,\label{E:phase-born}\\
  2171	    \|\E Z_2(h)\|_\lambda
  2172	    &\le\frac{D_\Gamma(1+\lambda^2h^2)h^{3-\alpha}}
  2173	    {\lambda(2-\alpha)(3-\alpha)}N.
  2174	    \label{E:phase-mean}
  2175	  \end{align}
  2176	  In particular, put $\lambda = h^{-1}$ and let $K_\epsilon$ be the coefficient
  2177	  of $\sigma^2$ in the finite polynomial $\E\|Z_0(h)+\sigma
  2178	  Z_1(h)+\sigma^2Z_2(h)\|_\lambda^2$. Then
  2179	  \begin{equation}\label{E:phase-variance}
  2180	    |K_\epsilon|
  2181	    \le\left(4R_\alpha+
  2182	    \frac{4\sqrt e\,D_\Gamma}{(2-\alpha)(3-\alpha)}\right)
  2183	    h^{4-\alpha}\|(f,g)\|_{1/h}^2.
  2184	  \end{equation}
  2185	\end{proposition}
  2186	
  2187	\begin{proof}
  2188	  We use the unnormalized spatial Fourier transform and Plancherel measure
  2189	  $(2\pi)^{-3}\ud\eta$. At fixed positive smoothing, Gaussian second and fourth
  2190	  moments make~\eqref{E:phase-duhamel} integrable: $G_t$ has finite positive
  2191	  mass, $C_t$ is an $L^2$ contraction, and $\E|W_\epsilon(x)W_\epsilon(y)|^2 \le
  2192	  3\Gamma_\epsilon(0)^2$. These facts, Minkowski and time integration justify
  2193	  the Gaussian and Fourier Fubini steps below first for Schwartz data.
  2194	
  2195	  Set $a_s(\eta) = \widehat{w}_0(s,\eta)$ and
  2196	  \[
  2197	    e_\lambda(\eta)=|\widehat{f}(\eta)|^2+
  2198	    \frac{|\widehat{g}(\eta)|^2}{\lambda^2+|\eta|^2}.
  2199	  \]
  2200	  Cauchy--Schwarz on the two initial coordinates gives
  2201	  \[
  2202	    |a_s(\eta)|^2\le(1+\lambda^2s^2)e_\lambda(\eta),
  2203	  \]
  2204	  because the squared norm of their coefficient vector is
  2205	  $\cos^2(sq)+(1+\lambda^2/q^2)\sin^2(sq) \le 1+\lambda^2s^2$, with the
  2206	  continuous value at $q = 0$. For the two-component output multiplier put
  2207	  \[
  2208	    k_\tau(r)=\left(\frac{\sin(\tau r)}r,
  2209	    \frac{\cos(\tau r)}{\sqrt{\lambda^2+r^2}}\right).
  2210	  \]
  2211	  Its Euclidean squared norm is
  2212	  \[
  2213	    |k_\tau(r)|^2
  2214	    =\frac{1+\lambda^2\sin^2(\tau r)/r^2}{\lambda^2+r^2}
  2215	    \le\frac{1+\lambda^2h^2}{\lambda^2+r^2},\qquad 0\le\tau\le h.
  2216	  \]
  2217	  Expanding the covariance of the two copies of $W_\epsilon$, followed by
  2218	  spatial Plancherel, gives exactly
  2219	  \[
  2220	    \E\|Z_1(h)\|_\lambda^2
  2221	    =\frac1{(2\pi)^3}\int\ud\eta\int\mu_\epsilon(\ud\xi)
  2222	    \left|\int_0^h k_{h-s}(|\eta+\xi|)a_s(\eta)\ud s\right|^2.
  2223	  \]
  2224	  Cauchy--Schwarz in time bounds the last squared norm by
  2225	  \[
  2226	    \frac{h^2(1+\lambda^2h^2)^2}
  2227	    {\lambda^2+|\eta+\xi|^2}e_\lambda(\eta).
  2228	  \]
  2229	  Now $\mu_\epsilon \le \mu$ and Lemma~\ref{L:phase-contractions}
  2230	  give~\eqref{E:phase-born}.
  2231	
  2232	  The contraction inside the mean of $Z_2$ is the convolution operator with
  2233	  kernel $G_{s-r}(\ud x)\Gamma_\epsilon(x)$. Indeed, this follows directly from
  2234	  $\E[W_\epsilon(x)W_\epsilon(y)] = \Gamma_\epsilon(x-y)$ in the two Duhamel
  2235	  integrals. Its Fourier multiplier is $T_\epsilon(s-r,\eta)$, up to the
  2236	  immaterial even sign. Its $L^2$ operator norm is therefore at most
  2237	  $D_\Gamma(s-r)^{1-\alpha}$. Under the isometry
  2238	  $(u,v)\mapsto(u,A_\lambda^{-1/2}v)$, $\|k_\tau(|D|)\|_{L^2\to L^2\oplus L^2}
  2239	  \le \sqrt{1+\lambda^2h^2}/\lambda$ and $\|w_0(r)\|_2 \le
  2240	  \sqrt{1+\lambda^2h^2}N$. Minkowski and
  2241	  \[
  2242	    \int_0^h\ud s\int_0^s(s-r)^{1-\alpha}\ud r
  2243	    =\frac{h^{3-\alpha}}{(2-\alpha)(3-\alpha)}
  2244	  \]
  2245	  prove~\eqref{E:phase-mean}.
  2246	
  2247	  Finally, the free phase obeys $\|Z_0(h)\|_\lambda \le e^{\lambda h/2}N$. To
  2248	  see this, for Schwartz free data differentiate its squared norm. The $-\Delta$
  2249	  terms cancel, leaving $2\lambda^2\operatorname{Re}\langle
  2250	  A_\lambda^{-1}\dot{w}_0,w_0\rangle$, whose absolute value is at most
  2251	  $\lambda\|Z_0\|_\lambda^2$. Gronwall gives the stated bound. The required
  2252	  coefficient is exactly
  2253	  \[
  2254	    K_\epsilon=\E\|Z_1(h)\|_\lambda^2+
  2255	    2\operatorname{Re}\langle Z_0(h),\E Z_2(h)\rangle_\lambda.
  2256	  \]
  2257	  Substituting $\lambda = h^{-1}$ into the two estimates proves
  2258	  \eqref{E:phase-variance}. This proves
  2259	  Proposition~\ref{P:static-phase-variance}.
  2260	\end{proof}

    46	    cut (truncC Nc) (fun i v => gmul i (fun l => K i (v l))) (fun b v => fun l => T b (v l))
    47	        (vac u) w =
    48	      raw (fun i v => gmul i (fun l => K i (v l))) (fun b v => fun l => T b (v l)) (vac u) w :=

    50	    (fun d i v hv => goodDeg_insert K d i v hv) (fun d b v hv => goodDeg_frame (T b) d v hv)
